answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to forge by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond before it can vote on transactions or earn trust. A zephyr account with no history starts with little influence; to build credibility, it must complete verifiable work over time, while fraud triggers slashing of its bond. Spawning a swarm of saffron and willow identities therefore multiplies the capital tied up and the risk of losing it, rather than granting an attacker free influence.
